title: Temperature Functions
story: Your cousin lives in London (Celsius) and you're in New York (Fahrenheit). Every weather chat turns into a math problem. Time to build a converter that does it automatically!
why: Real-world unit conversions are perfect for practicing functions that take a value, transform it with a formula, and return the result.
analogy: Temperature functions are like a universal power adapter — they convert one standard into another so everything works together.
try_it: Add a `c_to_k` function that converts Celsius to Kelvin (C + 273.15). Then write `describe_temp` that prints all three scales for a given Celsius value.
tips: Use `Float64` for temperatures — many conversions produce decimal values
Always use decimal points in floating-point literals: `9.0 / 5.0` not `9 / 5`
Write the formula EXACTLY as math dictates, using parentheses to control order
common_mistakes: Using `Int` instead of `Float64` — `9 / 5` in Int division gives `1`, not `1.8`
Getting the formula order wrong — multiplication before addition: `C * 9/5 + 32` not `C + 32 * 9/5`
Forgetting decimal points: `9/5` is integer division; `9.0/5.0` is float division
